title: Google basically confirms the Pixel 11 is getting a price hike
summary: Google's VP of Devices and Services confirms the Pixel 11 will cost more than its predecessor, attributing the hike to soaring RAM costs driven by AI data center expansion. Major tech companies including Apple and Microsoft have similarly raised prices due to memory supply constraints.
content:
Google's Vice President of Devices and Services, Shakil Barkat, all but confirmed in an interview with 9to5 Google that its next Pixel phone would cost more than the Pixel 10. Considering the ongoing RAM supply issues due to the explosion of AI data centers, the rumored price hike is not a complete surprise. Companies from Apple to Nintendo, Microsoft to Roku, have all raised their prices in response to the soaring cost of memory. 
Barkat said that Google had "shielded our consumers from supply fluctuations for as long as possible," but that the "economics have fundamentally shifted and we're not immune to that." He went on to tell 9to5 tha …
Read the full story at The Verge.

title: Synth historian Oli Freke will spend big on a good bicycle
summary: Synth historian and musician Oli Freke, known for works on synthesizer evolution and music theory, is launching Beat Gems, a visual coffee-table book documenting drum machine history through Bjooks. The project builds on Freke's scholarly approach to electronic music documentation.
content:
Oli Freke is a musician and journalist whose works have appeared in Sound on Sound, The Quietus, and Mixmag. This has included using math to explore the melodic potential of the Western 12-tone scale and deep dives on effects plug-ins. He's even written a book tracing the evolution of the synthesizer from 1963 through 1995, charting the change from analog to digital and back. 
His new project is Beat Gems, a coffee-table visual history of drum machines from publisher Bjooks. Like other Bjooks titles, Beat Gems is loaded with gorgeous photos, fascinating historical tidbits, and practical advice for making the most of your gear, whether it's  …

title: Teenage Engineering’s unique music machines are 30 percent off
summary: Teenage Engineering's music production devices, including the OP-XY synthesizer and EP-40 Riddim sampler, are discounted 30 percent across multiple retailers through early August. The OP-XY, normally $2,299, is reduced to $1,609.30, making premium music production tools more accessible.
content:
Teenage Engineering’s OP-XY has a huge number of functions. | Photo by Terrence O’Brien / The Verge	

With elements from synthesizers, loopers, and effects pedals, Teenage Engineering’s devices lie somewhere between musical instrument and modern art. These grooveboxes, as they’re often called, are capable of helping you produce songs in real time from a single unit, with an eye-catching design language. A wide swath of the brand’s offerings are 30 percent off at Guitar Center when you use code TE30, at Amazon when you click the on-page coupon for whichever product you’re interested in, and B&H Photo (discount applied automatically at checkout). The terms for the Amazon coupon claim it will run through August 8th, 2026, while Guitar Center deal is listed as “limited time.”
The OP-XY is one of the flagship units, which my colleague Terrence O’Brien described as a “greatest hits tour for Teenage Engineering.” Normally $2,299, the discount code brings the price down to a more palatable $1,609.30, which is a lot cheaper, but still pretty pricey for an aspiring musician. That said, it’s loaded with features for both production and live performance, and has a premium, durable build quality that reflects its price point. It’s currently sold out at Amazon, but in stock and discounted at Guitar Center and B&H Photo. Read our Teenage Engineering OP-XY review. 
Teenage Engineering OP-XY

Where to Buy:

 $2299 $1609.3 at B&H Photo
 $2299 $1609.3 at Guitar Center

The model I’m most tempted by is the EP-40 Riddim, a compact sampler with a library of over 400 built-in synth settings and effects particularly well-suited for producing dub and reggae music, plus 128MB of storage for your own loops and recorded sounds. It’s a bit less intimidating for a beginner than the OP-XY, both in terms of price point and features, and its tighter genre focus may help concentrate your efforts and onboarding. title: Is this e-reader case a gun?
summary: A creator designed a 3D-printed, pistol-shaped case for the Xteink X4 e-reader, called the "Gundle," that sparked debate about unconventional tech accessories. Though modeled after a real firearm, the case is non-functional and serves purely as a protective cover. The design highlights how maker communities are pushing boundaries in accessory form and function.
content:
Is an e-reader case as dangerous as a Glock 19? 
Last month, Louisville, Kentucky-based creator Luke The Maker showed off a bizarre, 3D-printed, pistol-shaped case design for the popular minimalist Xteink X4 e-reader. The X4 lies vertically atop the plastic gun's slide, with a cutout on the side to access its buttons. Though the frame was digitally modeled after a real gun, this "case" can't shoot bullets. Squeezing the trigger does nothing at all. He calls his contraption the "Gundle."

title: What Surrounds Us will make you think a lot about circles
summary: "What Surrounds Us" is a puzzle-adventure game where players control sentient circles navigating a world composed entirely of circular shapes and environments. The game explores themes of connection and collaboration between characters and their environment. The distinctive circular aesthetic reinforces the core message about working together within a larger ecosystem.
content:
What Surrounds Us takes its title literally. You play as a circle surrounding a hole in its middle - it looks like a donut with frosting. You work together with other sentient moving circles, sometimes helping them joyfully meet with others. And you traverse a large map that's composed entirely of, you guessed it, a series of circles. But the circles everywhere aren't just an artistic choice; they underscore the game's themes about working in connection with the environment and the things around us.
Despite the trippy design, What Surrounds Us has a familiar format. I kept feeling echoes of The Legend of Zelda as I trekked across three dist …

title: Forget expensive sleepbuds. Buy this pillow instead

This addresses the growing market of expensive audio sleep gadgets with a simpler, more durable approach.
content:
This “piercing pillow” also works great with earbuds you probably already own.	

Tech companies love to sell us expensive gadgets to solve all of life's little problems. Sleepbuds sold by the likes of Anker and Ozlo are a good example. These miniature marvels of engineering sit flush in the ear, and allow side-sleepers to doze off listening to podcasts, audiobooks, music, or white noise without annoying their partner. But why pay over $200 for a second pair of highly specialized buds when you can spend a fraction of that for a product that never needs charging, never loses its Bluetooth connection, and won't need replacing in a few years after the battery wears out?
